gaps.sentence: The factory laid ___ two hundred workers.
gaps.explanation: lay off = dismiss workers because there is not enough work.

gaps.sentence: They've set ___ a new charity for homeless dogs.
The plane will drop ___ the parcels at the next farm.
gaps.explanation: drop off = deliver somebody/something; also become less (sales dropped off).

gaps.sentence: After twenty years of smoking, he finally managed to give it ___.
gaps.explanation: give up = stop/quit (a habit or attempt).

gaps.sentence: It's time you faced up ___ your responsibilities.
gaps.explanation: face up TO something = accept and deal with something difficult.

gaps.sentence: The store decided to branch ___ into online sales.
gaps.explanation: branch out = start doing something new and different.

gaps.sentence: The match was called ___ because of the storm.
I've mixed ___ the twins' names again.
gaps.explanation: mix up = confuse one thing/person with another.
